---
title: "CPU, Metal, and CUDA"
---

## Backend contract {#sec-backend-contract}

| Backend | Active project | Production precision | Transform path |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPU | `.` | Float32; Float64 reference available | Native FFTW real transforms |
| Metal | `environments/metal` | Float32 only | MPSGraph real FFT for native Metal paths |
| CUDA | `environments/cuda` | Float32 runner | Native cuFFT real transforms |

The libraries have broader low-level capabilities than the production runner.
In particular, a CUDA-capable array type accepting Float64 does not make
`run.precision="f64"` a supported GPU production configuration. Device extensions
register backends only after the GPU package has loaded on functional hardware.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/src/MHDKernels.jl" "function backend" >}}

## Parallel CPU {#sec-cpu}

```sh
julia --project=. -t auto scripts/bootstrap.jl --backend=cpu
PMF_FFTW_THREADS=4 julia --project=. -t auto scripts/run_pmf.jl \
  examples/smoke.toml --backend=cpu --output=results/cpu-threads
```

`-t auto` supplies Julia threads to the CPU KernelAbstractions backend. It is
not MPI and does not distribute a job across nodes. `PMF_FFTW_THREADS` controls
FFTW independently; the launcher defaults to `min(4, Threads.nthreads())`.
Benchmark several Julia/FFTW thread combinations instead of assuming that the
largest count is fastest. Avoid running several all-core jobs simultaneously.
{{< src "scripts/_production.jl" "FFTW.set_num_threads" >}}

For a roundoff/reference comparison, set `run.precision="f64"` with CPU. Some
diagnostic and initialization paths still use Float32 intermediates; a CPU-f64
run is not proof that every operation is double precision.

## Apple Metal {#sec-metal}

Use Apple Silicon and a macOS/Metal stack supported by the resolved `Metal.jl`
version. The GPU environment is separate and includes all active-root local
source declarations.

```sh
julia --project=. -t auto scripts/bootstrap.jl --backend=metal
julia --project=environments/metal -e 'using Metal; @assert Metal.functional(); Metal.versioninfo()'
julia --project=environments/metal -t auto scripts/run_pmf.jl \
  examples/smoke.toml --backend=metal --output=results/metal-first
julia --project=environments/metal -t auto scripts/test_gpu.jl --backend=metal
```

The GPU kernels and MPSGraph path use Float32; do not request Float64. Native
MPS FFTs are not interchangeable with CPU FFTW plans. The radiation extension
batches spatial FFTs over three axes, retaining the fourth dimension as a
channel batch; zero-offset staging avoids the documented nonzero-view-offset
hazard. These details are part of backend parity testing, not optional changes.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/ext/MHDKernelsMetalExt.jl" "_radiation_forward_batch!" >}}

Unified memory is shared with macOS and other applications. Measure live memory
at increasing grid sizes, including radiation, chemistry, projection, spectra,
and checkpoint peaks. Do not size a run from the nine MHD fields alone.

## NVIDIA CUDA {#sec-cuda}

Use an NVIDIA GPU and a driver compatible with the CUDA.jl version selected
by the GPU environment. Bootstrap installs Julia package/artifact dependencies,
not the system GPU driver.

```sh
julia --project=. -t auto scripts/bootstrap.jl --backend=cuda
julia --project=environments/cuda -e 'using CUDA; @assert CUDA.functional(); CUDA.versioninfo()'
julia --project=environments/cuda -t auto scripts/run_pmf.jl \
  examples/smoke.toml --backend=cuda --output=results/cuda-first
julia --project=environments/cuda -t auto scripts/test_gpu.jl --backend=cuda
```

The current CUDA MHD extension routes `impl=:auto` to the shared KA algorithm.
Its historical native `impl=:raw` kernel is disabled because it predates the
current Riemann/source-aware interface. Radiation FFT plans on `CuArray`
dispatch to cuFFT, including the channel batch. Explicit portable gravity FFT
options remain available and have different performance characteristics.
{{< src "lib/MHDKernels/ext/MHDKernelsCUDAExt.jl" "_radiation_forward_batch!" >}}

::: {.callout-warning}
## Hardware validation is a separate gate
These are installation and test instructions, not a claim of CUDA hardware
validation. Check the [recorded results](test-results.qmd). A skipped GPU test,
CPU parity test, or successfully imported CUDA package is not a passing CUDA run.
:::

## Cluster and hardware CI {#sec-hardware-ci}

`examples/slurm-cuda.sh` launches one node with one GPU and threaded CPU
support. Adapt its account, partition, resource request, and job time to the
cluster. Bootstrap once before submitting, keep output on a sufficiently large
filesystem, and use a different run directory for every realization. Multiple
GPUs are not automatically combined into one simulation.

The manual **GPU hardware validation** GitHub Actions workflow uses a
self-hosted runner with labels `pmf-glm` and either `metal` or `cuda`. It runs
backend parity, full chemistry/photon/gravity smoke, and a warm MHD benchmark,
then uploads the actual evidence and resolved environment. It is dispatched
explicitly; pull requests do not execute on private GPU hosts. CPU CI runs
Linux/macOS with one and four threads. Configure a runner only after testing
the same local commands on that hardware.

## Selecting FFTs {#sec-fft-selection}

`[physics] fft="auto"` maps to `MHD_FFT=auto`. The extracted runner chooses
the **native real-FFT interface on all three backends**. Its internal/log label
is historically `mps`: this means MPSGraph on Metal, FFTW on CPU, and cuFFT on
CUDA, not Apple code running on an NVIDIA card. `mps`, `native`, and `rfft` are
aliases for that same native interface. `ka` is the portable real-FFT gravity
solver; `c2c` is the full-complex portable alternative.
{{< src "src/production/runner.jl" "function _fft_mode" >}}

Metal rejects a non-MPS gravity selection unless
`MHD_ALLOW_NON_MPS_FFT=1` is explicitly set. Such changes are benchmark
experiments. Preserve the transform choice, Green function, grid, precision,
thread count, and device information in every performance or parity comparison.
